newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton closes modestly up on moderate volume.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton closes modestly up on moderate volume.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled modestly higher on Friday as traders continued to roll their positions from May into July ahead of first notice day, floor sources said.
First notice day for the May contract is April 24.
Light local and trade buying lifted prices amid an estimated volume of 10,500 lots, traders said.
"It was a 50-point range day," one trader said, pointing out that open interest was very large.

"It was all switches because of first notice day coming next week," he said. "Everybody is in there. The open interest is very, very big, so we have a lot of rolling and that is all we seem to be doing," he said.

As of Friday morning, May's open interest was 17,019 lots and July's open interest was about 30,840 lots. This compares to the same time year-ago period of open interest in May which totalled 7,670 lots and July's open interest of 19,907 lots on April 19, 1996, another trader said.
May was up 0.11 cent at 70.86 cents a lb while the rest of the board 0.08 to 0.10 cent up.
